packages.name: sys-con
packages.title: sys-con
packages.description: Use USB controllers from other consoles on Nintendo Switch.
packages.author: cathery, o0Zz
packages.details:
sys-con is a Nintendo Switch sysmodule that adds support for third-party USB controllers.

It supports a wide range of HID and XInput-compatible gamepads, including PlayStation, Xbox, PC controllers, arcade sticks, wheels, and other USB input devices. Controllers can be used in docked mode or through a compatible USB-C OTG adapter in handheld mode.

Configuration files under `sd:/config/sys-con/` allow you to customize button mappings, stick and trigger behavior, deadzones, polling settings, controller profiles, and other device-specific options.
packages.changelog:
2.0.0

# Changelog
 - Implemented MITM mode
 - Added Rumble support
 - Added Gyro support
 - Added SInput support
 - Added support for UDP network controllers
 - Drastically reduced sys-con's RAM and ROM footprint

This release is a major update of sys-con, with a large portion of the codebase refactored and improved.
Because of the scale of these changes, this version may be less stable than previous releases. If stability is your priority, consider staying on v1.7.0 for now.

Special thanks to @saad-script for their help with development and testing.

packages.name: sys-patch
packages.title: sys-patch
packages.description: Apply system patches automatically at boot.
packages.author: btc08gh, impeeza
packages.details:
sys-patch is a Nintendo Switch sysmodule that automatically applies fs, es, ldr, nifm, and nim patches when the system boots.

It can patch both sysMMC and emuMMC and includes an overlay for changing configuration options and checking which patches were successfully applied. The overlay distinguishes between patches applied by sys-patch and patches that were already present from another source.

Configuration is stored in `sd:/config/sys-patch/config.ini`, where you can control sysMMC and emuMMC patching, logging, and version-pattern behavior.

Because sys-patch modifies low-level system behavior, it is best suited for advanced users who understand Atmosphere and firmware compatibility.

packages.name: nx-fancontrol
packages.title: NX-FanControl
packages.description: Custom fan curve control for Nintendo Switch.
packages.author: Zathawo, dominatorul
packages.details:
NX-FanControl is a Nintendo Switch sysmodule and overlay for customizing the console's internal fan curve.

It allows you to define multiple temperature points with corresponding fan speeds, giving you more control over the balance between cooling performance and fan noise. The overlay also provides real-time monitoring of SoC temperature and fan RPM.

Because NX-FanControl directly changes fan behavior, use sensible fan curves and avoid settings that significantly reduce cooling at high temperatures.
packages.changelog:
1.0.5+

Added

Support for 10 fan curve points, giving finer control over fan behavior.
SoC temperature and Fan Speed readings in the overlay.

Changed

Removed fan level change threshold — Fan speed now updates every cycle, giving immediate response to temperature or setting changes.

~Reduced sleep time from 500ms to 250ms — Updates 4 times per second, providing a more responsive experience while staying efficient.~

Optimized sleep state checking — System sleep is now checked every 20 iterations (~5 seconds) instead of every loop, reducing overhead while keeping power-saving functionality.

Fixed

Various minor bug fixes for improved stability and reliability.

Recompiled for latest Atmosphere support

2/13/2026

Reduced heap size from 512kb to 50kb. Now it uses 10x less memory.
Reduced sleep time to 50 ms and for temps over 50 degrees to 25ms.
Fixed critical config corruption bug: corrected fwrite/fread parameter order so fan curves now save/load properly.
Fixed fan speed not updating due to hysteresis logic: fan now updates immediately.
Removed unused variables causing Werror build failures.

packages.name: prelude
packages.title: Prelude
packages.description: Switch between Nextendo Network and Nintendo's official network services.
packages.author: Nextendo Network
packages.details:
Prelude is a Nintendo Switch homebrew application for switching an Atmosphere console between Nextendo Network and Nintendo's official network services.

Nextendo mode configures the Atmosphere files and patches needed to connect supported games and services to Nextendo Network. Nintendo mode removes Prelude's changes and restores the console's normal Nintendo network configuration.

Prelude applies its changes through files and settings that Atmosphere reads at boot, making the process reversible. After selecting a network mode, the console reboots so the new configuration can take effect.
packages.changelog:
v3.5.15

## Prelude v3.5.15

**New: Dragon Ball FighterZ online on Nextendo.**

- Redirects Bandai Namco's API host (`dbf.channel.or.jp`) to Nextendo. The game signs in there before any other online traffic, so without this line it reaches Bandai's real server, is refused, and shows "Failed to initialize network".
- Adds the explicit NEX host for the game's lobby (`g21b61a00-lp1.s.n.srv.nintendo.net`), next to the other per-game NEX entries.
- No ExeFS patches are needed.
- Update, open Prelude once in Nextendo mode to apply the hosts, then **fully power off and restart** the console (the hosts file is only read at boot).
- Requires Dragon Ball FighterZ 1.50 and a linked Nextendo account.

Known issues: lobbies can be entered, but Arena Match does not start a match yet, and the "Latest News" panel is empty. Both are being worked on server-side; no Prelude update will be needed for them.

Full changelog: https://github.com/NextendoNetwork/Prelude-Nextendo/compare/v3.5.14...v3.5.15

packages.name: reversenx-rt
packages.title: ReverseNX-RT
packages.description: Switch between handheld and docked modes in real time.
packages.author: masagrator, ppkantorski
packages.details:
ReverseNX-RT is an Ultrahand overlay that lets you switch compatible Nintendo Switch games between handheld and docked rendering modes in real time.

It is useful for forcing a game's handheld or docked graphics profile without rebooting the console or restarting the game, allowing you to compare image quality, resolution, performance, and power behavior on the fly.

This build is maintained by ppkantorski and rebuilt with libultrahand for integration with the modern Ultrahand overlay ecosystem.

packages.title: 90DNS Tester
packages.description: Test whether Nintendo network services are blocked.
packages.author: meganukebmp
packages.details:
90DNS Tester checks network connectivity from your Nintendo Switch to determine whether Nintendo services are being successfully blocked.

It is useful for verifying 90DNS-style DNS configurations and other network setups intended to prevent connections to Nintendo's servers while retaining general internet access.

packages.name: sys-dock
packages.title: sys-dock
packages.description: Enable higher docked display bandwidth and refresh rates.
packages.author: masagrator
packages.details:
sys-dock is a Nintendo Switch sysmodule that patches docked DisplayPort link training to allow higher-bandwidth display modes and higher refresh rates.

It is primarily intended for use alongside FPSLocker, especially on OLED models where the default docked DisplayPort configuration can limit available refresh rates. The included overlay lets you enable or disable individual DisplayPort patches and see which patches are currently active.

Configuration is stored in `sd:/config/sys-dock/config.ini` and can be edited manually or through the overlay.

Because sys-dock changes low-level dock and display behavior, incompatible docks, displays, cables, or patch combinations may cause display corruption, instability, or other unexpected behavior.

It supports NXTheme packages as well as direct image installation and includes compatibility handling for different HOME Menu versions. Newer releases also support boot-screen installation and selective installation of images or layouts from NXTheme files.

packages.name: fpslocker
packages.title: FPSLocker
packages.description: An overlay that allows users to set custom FPS targets in retail games.
packages.author: masagrator
packages.details:
FPSLocker is an overlay that works with SaltyNX to set custom FPS targets and display refresh rates in Nintendo Switch games.

packages.name: ldn-mitm
packages.title: ldn_mitm
packages.description: Play local-wireless Nintendo Switch games over LAN.
packages.author: spacemeowx2, DefenderOfHyrule
packages.details:
ldn_mitm is an Atmosphere sysmodule that replaces the Nintendo Switch ldn service and redirects local-wireless discovery over LAN networking.

It allows games that normally communicate through local wireless to work over a network connection, and is commonly used together with switch-lan-play for online play with supported local-wireless titles.

The package also includes configuration tools and should be rebooted after installation so the sysmodule can start.

packages.name: tico
packages.title: tico
packages.description: A customizable multi-system game launcher and emulator frontend.
packages.author: tico
packages.details:
tico is a Nintendo Switch game launcher and emulator frontend with support for multiple retro systems through independently maintained emulator cores.

It provides a customizable home interface, game-library browsing, cover and artwork management, RetroAchievements integration, touch support, and built-in management for supported emulator cores.

Additional emulator cores and supporting files can be installed or updated from within tico.
packages.changelog:
0.7.9

## What's New
### Batch Asset Downloads
* Added the ability to batch download covers, backgrounds, logos, and icons for your entire game library.
---
### New Customization Options
Take control of Tico's look and startup experience with several new personalization settings:
* **Skip the screen transition animation** for an instant switch between screens.
* **Customize the screen tint color**, affecting both the dock and the startup animation.
* **Change the tint color of inactive dock items** to better match your theme.
* **Customize the animated gradient border** with your preferred color.
* **Choose your startup screen**, launching directly into either **Home** or **Game Select**
---
### Homescreen & Backgrounds
* Added the option to use the game background as the homescreen background.
* Added per-screen homescreen backgrounds.
* Added a symbol decoration for console card home shortcuts.
* Added an optional background overlay for the homescreen — a semi-transparent white/black layer that improves the visibility of components above it.
* Added new background animations for Home and Game Select, which can be set individually per screen.
---
### Homescreen Cards
* Added styled console and game cards to the homescreen, each with a frame and badges available at all card sizes. Styled items can be disabled individually to show the raw item as before.
* Added **1×2** and **2×1** item size options, giving you more flexibility when organizing your layout.
---
### Interface Settings Refactor
The Interface settings have been reorganized into clearer sections:
* **Animations** — Skip animation, and Screen transition animation (used when the intro isn't skipped).
* **Screens** — Separate settings for Home (game backgrounds, background transition, theme overlay, and other previously available options) and Game Select (background transition, theme overlay, and other previously available options).
* **Card Settings** — Console and game card customization, now organized into sections, with a new option to extend card styling to the homescreen.
* **Tint** — Screen tint color, inactive dock item tint, and gradient border color.
---
### Interface & Navigation
* Improved the Quick Menu with per-screen options and a new layout.
* Improved the Retro Achievements screen layout, with a new per-console view.
* Added touch support to previously unsupported screens, including Assets and others.
* Added the option to rescan all consoles at once.
---
## Want to Contribute?

Every emulator core has its own repository under the **Tico GitHub organization**, making development, issue tracking, and contributions easier.

Bug reports, feature requests, and pull requests are always welcome. Please respect each core's original license and attribution requirements.

---

packages.name: sys-tune
packages.title: sys-tune
packages.description: Background audio player for Nintendo Switch.
packages.author: HookedBehemoth, ppkantorski
packages.details:
sys-tune is a background audio player for Nintendo Switch with an Ultrahand overlay for controlling playback.

It supports MP3, FLAC, and WAV audio, playlist browsing, seeking, shuffle and repeat modes, persistent playback settings, per-title behavior, and separate control over music and game audio volume.

Music can be played from the SD card and managed without leaving the currently running game or application. sys-tune can also be configured for HOME Menu background music and title-specific playback behavior.

Because audio playback can interfere with sleep mode or titles that heavily use the system audio renderer, pause playback or stop the service if you encounter audio or sleep-related issues.

packages.name: saltynx
packages.title: SaltyNX
packages.description: Background process for the Nintendo Switch for file/code modification.
packages.author: shinyquagsire23, masagrator
packages.details:
SaltyNX is a background process for Nintendo Switch that enables runtime file and code modification in retail games.

Originally created by shinyquagsire23 and maintained as an expanded fork by masagrator, SaltyNX provides the underlying framework used by tools such as FPSLocker and other game-modification plugins.

This fork includes numerous quality-of-life, compatibility, performance-monitoring, display-control, and plugin-injection improvements.

packages.details:
Virtual amiibo (amiibo emulation) system for Nintendo Switch.

Virtual amiibos are stored under `sd:/emuiibo/amiibo` and should be organized into subdirectories. emuiibo intercepts the Switch's amiibo services, allowing compatible games to use virtual amiibos through its overlay.

Use the emuiibo overlay to enable or disable amiibo emulation, select an active virtual amiibo, connect or disconnect it, and configure options such as randomized UUIDs.

packages.name: missioncontrol
packages.title: MissionControl
packages.description: Use controllers from other consoles via Bluetooth.
packages.author: ndeadly
packages.details:
Use controllers from other consoles natively on your Nintendo Switch via Bluetooth. No dongles or other external hardware necessary.

After installing this package, reboot your console to activate the module.

MissionControl supports a wide range of Bluetooth controllers, including Wii/Wii U, DualShock 3/4, DualSense, Xbox One Bluetooth controllers, several 8BitDo models, and many third-party controllers. It integrates with the Switch's native controller pairing and remapping interfaces, supports rumble and motion controls on compatible devices, and can connect multiple non-Switch Bluetooth controllers simultaneously.
packages.changelog:
v0.16.0

This release adds support for firmware 23.0.0/23.0.1, adds a new setting for Dualsense adaptive trigger travel distance and fixes several outstanding issues. See below for full changelog. _Note: the codebase has undergone some non-trivial refactoring since the previous release. While most of the changes shouldn't result in any noticable differences to the end user, there is the possibility that new issues have been introduced into code that was previously stable. I tried to get users in my discord server to help test to ensure the new release was as bug free as possible, but was met with a rather underwhelming response. Since I can't hold up the release for 23.0.0 indefinitely I am releasing in its current state. Please look out for and report any regressions you may come across, and if you value timely and stable future releases, consider subscribing to notifications in the #testing channel of my discord server and helping out._ New users landing on this release page should first check out the readme on the [main project page](https://github.com/ndeadly/MissionControl#readme) for the official project documentation. There you can find installation and usage instructions along with an FAQ section that will answer most of your questions. ### Changelog - Added full support for firmware 23.0.0/23.0.1 - Added a feature for setting the maximum travel distance of Dualsense adaptive triggers - Modified device class check patch to allow JoyconDroid (non-root) to accept a broader range of devices - Reworked battery level reporting for Sony controllers to be more accurate and avoid warning notifications when the level is not critically low - Added mitm for shortened versions of btm GetDeviceCondition and GetDeviceInfo functions - Fixed a bug where the priority of the bluetooth event mitm thread was lower than it should have been - Miscellaneous internal changes to improve accuracy and coverage of controller protocol implementation

packages.name: status-monitor-deux
packages.title: Status Monitor Deux
packages.description: Monitor Nintendo Switch hardware statistics in real time.
packages.author: masagrator
packages.details:
Status Monitor Deux is the next generation of Status Monitor Overlay for Nintendo Switch.

It displays real-time hardware statistics such as per-core CPU usage, GPU load, CPU/GPU/RAM frequencies, memory usage, temperatures, and fan behavior through an overlay interface.

Unlike the original Status Monitor Overlay, Status Monitor Deux uses customizable `.smd` script files for its display modes and `.smse` extension files for additional services, giving you much more control over how information is presented.

Its configuration, modes, extensions, and localization files are stored under `sd:/config/status-monitor-deux`.
